A Parameter-Free Candidate for the Fine-Structure Constant from Entangled Qudits A. D. Wissner-Gross∗ (Dated: October 23, 2026)

We derive an exact candidate for the fine-structure constant α(0) from one parameter-free quantum-information axiom: nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of finitedimensional systems, some shared, known only by distilling them. Its one readable link with an acting central charge, a qutrit with a qubit,√ has the √ Standard √ Model gauge group (SU (3) × SU (2) × U (1))/Z6 and two-point function (79 + 48 2 + 42 3 + 3 6)/31104 = 1/137.035 999 190 . . .. We conjecture that this link is the elementary link of the photon, making the number α(0), 0.6σ from CODATA 2022. Lean 4 checks the computation.

Introduction.—The fine-structure constant at zero momentum transfer, α(0), is known to a tenth of a part per billion [1–4], yet the Standard Model takes it from experiment. A derivation of α(0) would, almost by definition, draw on physics beyond the Standard Model, and the precision of the measurements, about ten significant figures for any candidate to match, could make α(0) an exquisite probe of that physics. Proposed closed forms for α(0) have a long history, and the serious ones foundered on what fixed their normalization, since the volume of a symmetric domain can be rescaled, and with it the number [5–8]. A derivation of α(0) must therefore exhibit its one input and leave nothing to fix.

Axiom. Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them.

Definitions. A qudit is a finite-dimensional quantum system, of dimension at least two, since a onedimensional system cannot be entangled and so ends no pair. A pair, or link, of type (d1 , d2 ) joins qudits of dimensions d1 and d2 in the maximally entangled state on their common support, of dimension m = min(d1 , d2 ),

It must also compute the right quantity, and the onshell scheme of quantum electrodynamics says which. For a massless spin-one field coupled to a conserved abelian charge, the coupling at zero transfer is universal [9, 10]; the Ward identity Z1 = Z2 , equating the renormalizations of the vertex and of the charged field, reduces it to the vacuum polarization, α(0) = Z3 αbare , with Z3 the renormalization of the gauge field and αbare the bare coupling [11]; and charged states of any mass decouple from this limit [12]. One needs exactly one object with (i) a conserved abelian charge obeying a Ward identity and (ii) a two-point function with its pole at zero transfer, and then (iii) its dressed-over-bare two-point function at that pole, the ratio of residues that is Z3 .

A qudit is shared when it is an end of two or more pairs. Because a pure maximally entangled pair is uncorrelated with every third system, a shared qudit is carried as one copy per pair, each maximally entangled with its own partner, as in a projected entangled pair state [25], so monogamy is never violated. These are copies of a qudit, one per pair, not copies of a link, of which there is only ever one. The copies are still one qudit, the one the axiom shares, so exchanging two pairs at a shared qudit leaves it in place and moves only what sits at their far ends. To distill two qudits is to project them onto Pm = |ωm ⟩⟨ωm |, and its output is the pair of their type.

Here, distilling generalizes entanglement distillation, which extracts maximally entangled pairs from many copies of a less entangled state by local operations and classical communication [26, 27]. But every state is already maximally entangled, so there is nothing for copies or local operations to purify, and what remains is a single joint projection onto the pair state, on one copy and with no failure branch. It is the projection of entanglement swapping [28], which between pairs moves entanglement and adds none. In a laboratory, the same projection is a postselection, one outcome of a Bell measurement, obtained between two pairs of dimension d with probability 1/d2 . In our model, the complementary outcome is no configuration of the axiom, so the projection is the act itself. Postselection has been proposed as a law before, for the final state of black holes and for closed timelike curves [29, 30].

Three facts suggest where to look. First, a bounded region holds finitely many degrees of freedom [13–15], and quantum theory and gravitation have both been reconstructed from information and entanglement [16– 19]. Second, the Standard Model gauge group (SU (3) × SU (2) × U (1))/Z6 is generated by local basis changes at the two ends of a qutrit maximally entangled with a qubit, namely SU (3) at one end, SU (2) at the other, and a relative phase that neither end owns. Third, bound entanglement, certifiable but undistillable, first becomes possible when the product of the two dimensions exceeds six [20–23], the bound beyond which positive maps between two systems need not decompose. Taken literally, in the spirit of Wheeler’s “it from bit” [24], they combine into a single axiom.

Each pair has its own matching, so nothing lines up the bases of a shared qudit’s copies. A read is an act at one end of a pair, the end at which it is taken. It distills the two ends in a basis of that end and passes the basis along the pair, leaving the far end at each element |e⟩ in ⟨e|ωm ⟩, the conjugate of the part of |e⟩ on the support, with no freedom. The basis it passes reaches the far end whole, but these states span only the support, so a read is taken at the larger end of a pair, or at either end when the two are equal. At an end of prime dimension d, such as a qubit or a qutrit, there is one read for each of the d + 1 mutually unbiased bases of the clock and shift operators [31]. The traceless parts of their projectors, d − 1 per basis, are mutually orthogonal, so no read repeats another, and together span all (d + 1)(d − 1) = d2 − 1 traceless observables of that end, three at a qubit (the Pauli matrices) and eight at a qutrit (the Gell-Mann matrices).

To fix is to determine with certainty from a single copy, not to estimate an expectation value over many. Certainty leaves nothing open, so a read fixes two ends only when every consistent relation between them, a positive map between their operator algebras, is of a kind distillations carry. What is known of a qudit is what its reads fix jointly, under every matching of its pairs and every exchange of its reads or of its pairs. Two reads fix their product jointly, and exchanging them returns the product times the phase by which they fail to commute. An exchange done twice is no exchange, so that phase must be a sign, and two anticommuting reads thus fix one thing more than either alone, their product, with their order as its sign. These five definitions, of a qudit, sharing, distilling, a read, and the known, spell out the axiom’s terms, and their properties follow from it (Supplemental Material [32], Sec. S1).

Measurement.—Three consequences of the axiom settle our model’s measurement theory. A configuration is a set of links, some of them read, and its readout is the number its reads deliver. First, the pair state is unchanged, or envariant [33], under every matching, so every readout is invariant under their average, the isotropic twirl. Second, the pairs are finitely many and distilling creates no qudit, so no link between the same two qudits exists twice. A read therefore acts once on the one copy of the link it reads, and what matters is what a single read fixes, not asymptotic distillability. Third, the operators invariant under every matching are spanned by 11 and Pm [34], so a read delivers its pair projector and nothing finer.

The readout is then a normalized trace over the readout algebra R, the operators the reads can reach, which are

the whole operator space of each read link and, since no read sees the scalar part of an unread link, the traceless part of each unread link. What the reads insert into a readout is an operator on R, an insertion, as an n-point function in field theory inserts n fields into a state. A configuration may carry any number of reads, and this Letter needs two, those of a two-point function. The on-shell scheme of the Introduction compares the dressed two-point function Gdressed , with every interaction, to the bare one Gbare , with none. Here the bare insertion is the identity of R, which weighs every direction of R once, and the dressed insertion M weighs only the directions the reads fix, each at the amplitude it carries through the pairs it runs over (Theorem 2 below). Which links can be read.—A read meets a pair ket, pure and maximally entangled, so its projection onto the pair succeeds with probability one on the single copy, and that certainty is the bare unit of the readout. No state of the model is bound entangled, since every link is a pure maximally entangled state, distillable in every dimension. What a read can fail to fix is therefore not a state but a relation between the two ends of a type. A consistent relation, a positive map between the operator algebras of two ends, carries every description of one end to a description of the other, and the matchings are its unitary cases. Reads carry operators across a link in two ways, directly by their projection and the matchings, which are completely positive, and to the far end by the transpose identity. Every map that reads compose is therefore decomposable, a completely positive map plus a completely positive map after the transpose [32]. Call a type readable when every positive map between its ends is decomposable, so that reads carry every consistent relation between them, and dark otherwise. By the definition of fix, a single read fixes the ends of a pair exactly when its type is readable. Every positive map is decomposable at (2, 2) [35] and (2, 3) [36]. Nondecomposable maps exist at (2, 4) [36] and (3, 3) [37], and they embed in every type with d1 d2 ≥ 8; no product of two integers ≥ 2 equals seven. So a type of dimensions d1 , d2 ≥ 2 is readable if and only if d1 d2 ≤ 6, the read cap, and the readable types are (2, 2) and (2, 3), of which (2, 3) alone has unequal ends.

Through the Choi–Jamiolkowski correspondence [38, 39], the maps reads cannot carry are the witnesses of entanglement with positive partial transpose [20, 21], which no standard distillation reaches [22], so a dark type has a sector that standard distillation never reaches, though each of its links stays maximally entangled. A second route gives the same cap, if the far end of a read must hold the passed basis as its own [32]. With reads taken at qubits and qutrits, a read spans no end of dimension four or more. The charge is conserved. Up to scale, the only functional of the open ends of a configuration that every matching preserves and that sees no global phase is the count of Q, and every read or join changes the open ends by a matched ket–bra pair, so the count is unchanged. The count sums to zero over all directions of the two ends, which is the tracelessness of Q, while the link matches one direction of each end, which is why Q acts on the pair ket as i. Because the twirl fixes Q, its dressed and bare insertions agree, Z1 = Z2 [32].

The conjecture and the comparison.—The object’s charge is the hypercharge direction. Its passage to electric charge, together with spacetime and helicity, lies beyond this Letter, so we state the identification as a conjecture and let the measured value test it. The identification is with α itself, the unit-free coupling per unit charge, not with e2 in a convention that carries 4π. Conjecture 1 (Photon). The qutrit–qubit link of Theorem 1 is the elementary link of the photon, and its dressed-over-bare readout αcand , Eq. (6), is the electromagnetic coupling at zero momentum transfer, α(0). The number is computed from the axiom, its five definitions, and the two definitions of the computed quantity, the two-point function and the normalized readout, and nothing in it is fit to α. decide the configuration and the weights, the on-shell definition names the result, and the conjecture identifies it. It is striking that an axiom about entangled pairs, which mentions neither charge nor spacetime, singles out the Standard Model gauge group and reaches α(0) at this precision. This is the first separately published result of Chain Theory, our broader program to study fundamental physics through the lens of quantum information. If the conjecture holds, α(0) is a weighted count over the 172 measurement records of one entangled pair, and the premise that fundamental physics arises from networks of entangled pairs may prove a fertile avenue toward physics beyond the Standard Model.

THE MODEL

The axiom reads: Nothing exists but finitely many maximally entangled pairs of qudits, some qudits shared, known only by distilling them. Its five definitions (qudit, shared, distilling, read, known) spell out its terms, and the properties of each that the Letter uses follow from it as the corollaries below. Lemma S1 supplies the matchings used in the first. Corollary S1 (A qudit). The state space of an end is the span of the outputs of the acts on it, the pair kets under the admissible matchings. At the qutrit–qubit link that span is the whole six-dimensional tensor space. The moduli of its inner products are fixed by the Born readout; their phases beyond the moduli are fixed by no readout. Proof. The acts on an end are distillations, whose outputs are pair kets on the common support, carried by the matchings over the orbit of the pair ket. At (2, 3) the orbit under the fourth-root matchings at both ends has 96 vectors and spans all 6 dimensions, as does the cyclic module generated from the pair ket by the matrix units of the two ends; the same holds at every type with ends of dimension two to four. The frame operator of the orbit is a scalar, so the Born readouts, the squared moduli of the Gram elements at all 576 pairs of the frame, fix the moduli of the inner products. The remaining phases are moved by matchings that fix every readout.

A pair of the axiom of type (d1 , d2 ), also called a link, joins two qudits of dimensions d1 , d2 in the pair ket on their common support, and distilling two qudits outputs the pair of their type. A qudit is shared when it is one end of two or more pairs, spelling out “some qudits shared”, and its copies, one per pair, are one qudit, so an exchange of its pairs leaves it in place and moves only their far ends.

The rank of every operator equals the Schmidt rank of its output across the cut, and Pm returns the pair, so the act is Pm and nothing else.

In the on-shell scheme the coupling is defined by two conditions: the residue of the propagator at the physical pole is one, and the vertex is taken at the pole. The ancillary file ChainAlpha.lean is a single Lean 4 file on the core library alone, with no Mathlib and no imports; lean ChainAlpha.lean checks it with Lean 4.35.0 in about a hundred seconds. Every computation is checked by the kernel. The file contains no sorry, no axiom declaration, and no native code. Its main theorem, ChainAlpha.main, has no hypotheses beyond the definitions of the file’s Part 1. It states that the object is a two-point configuration of the qutrit–qubit link, that reads at the qutrit fix the qubit while reads at the qubit do not fix the qutrit, that every record, built from the slots and the matrices, is an eigenvector of the exchange of the reads, and that √ commutator √ √ the normalized readout is (79 + 48 2 + 42 3 + 3 6)/31104. It depends on propositional extensionality alone. The √ file computes the two traces that define the readout, the sum of kr over the records and the readout dimension, without constructing the readout space itself.

The definitions of Part 1 are those of Table S1: the axiom as a structure of qudits and links; its five definitions, with the definition of fix and the three clauses of Table S1, from which the file builds the slots and their letters, the records with their own signs and the commutator records, the two exchanges and survival, and the weight function; and the two definitions of the computed quantity, the two-point configuration and the normalized readout. Outside comments, the digits 79, 48, 42, and 31104 and the counts 169 and 172 occur only in theorem statements, so they are outputs and not inputs. Table S6 maps the results of this paper to the declarations. The ancillary script mutations.py perturbs the definitions one at a time; every perturbation that changes a value at the object makes the main theorem or commutator_records fail.

Under the read cap, a named hypothesis that cites the theorems of Størmer, Woronowicz, and Choi in their numerical form for the definition of a readable type, selection_under_read_cap gives the qutrit–qubit link as the only readable type with an acting charge. The file also contains the readers remark of Sec. S2: readers_reproduce_ the_cap shows that readability by reads, with the qubit and the qutrit as readers and the far end absorbing the

23 conjugation, holds exactly when d1 d2 ≤ 6, so reads_satisfy_the_read_cap discharges the cap’s hypothesis for it; qubit_absorbs_conjugation and qutrit_conjugation_obstruction check the two facts about conjugation on the matching groups.
